_comment: Blueprint 16.2. Safety floors identical in all three - verified by the cross-profile parity test.

volume.source: R2 for daily volume (brief states 100-500+); peak factor 1.8x and off-peak 0.58x are ASM (Blueprint 7.1).

staffing.relooks_note: Blueprint 7.3: assumes a re-look takes ~3 minutes and a triage nurse can devote roughly half their time to reassessment. This single number derives K and therefore the entire attention budget, so it is exposed as configurable and its sensitivity is reported (Blueprint 23.3).
staffing.unknown_staffing_note: Blueprint complexity 12 fallback: unknown staffing -> assume the profile's declared minimum, which produces the most conservative (smallest) K and the earliest deficit warning.

capacity.boarding_note: Admitted patients occupying ED capacity. Enters as a CAPACITY REDUCER, never as a priority reducer (constraint C3).

capability_inventory.note: Blueprint complexity 11: routing recommendations are FILTERED against this inventory before display. An unavailable pathway becomes a TRANSFER-CONSIDERATION FLAG, not a silent omission. Unknown capability -> treat as unavailable and surface the transfer flag. Assume less, not more.

acuity_vocabulary.note: The AIIMS Triage Protocol deliberately uses three colour-coded categories with corresponding physical zones because of limited numbers of trained emergency staff. The WHO/MSF/ICRC integrated triage tool is likewise a three-tier traffic-light instrument for resource-limited settings [S12]. The engine reasons at five levels INTERNALLY and presents in whichever vocabulary the hospital uses.

protocol_floor_override_note: TIGHTEN ONLY. A hospital may require faster reassessment than the universal floor and never slower. Rejected at profile load with a named violation otherwise.
conformal_alpha_note: LOWER ONLY (more conservative). Bounded by the universal ceiling of 0.20.

patient_mix.note: Blueprint 7.2. Pre-hospital transport penetration is lower in district settings.

behaviour_difference_that_matters: K=1 means the board answers one question: who is the single next person to look at. Time-critical pathways surface as TRANSFER DECISIONS rather than internal routing. Level-2 protocol floor tightened to 10 min because there is one nurse and a missed re-look has no backstop.
